kevin: Quick heads-up — ran a few end-to-end profiles this morning against the 2.1 runtime builds. Observed a reproducible GPU mem spike tied to batch growth > 128 that leads to kernel fallback to the generic kernel and eventual OOM on 24GB nodes. nvprof traces attached in the CI artifact.
maya: ugh. do we have a short repro? can you paste the top-level alloc stack or the CLI you used? :eyes:
kevin: repro is tiny: 1) run the loadgen with sequence length distribution skewed toward long tails (2048), 2) set batching cap to 512, 3) enable kv-cache + workspace_reuse=false. Command:

```
./loadgen --model gptx-6B --seq-dist long_tail.json --max-batch 512 --kv=true --workspace_reuse=false --iters 1000
```
kevin: nvprof summary: 12% extra resident from per-seq temp buffers, plus 18% due to fallback generic kernel using larger ephemeral buffers. Timeline shows KV eviction churn right before the fallback.
sanjay: interesting — sounds like two compounding issues: allocator fragmentation from variable workspace requests + kernel selection heuristic that prefers single-call generic kernels once memory pressure seen. we should try lowering the batch growth predictor so it pads less aggressively.
maya: can we try `workspace_reuse=true` + tuned watermarks before changing allocator? that might be lowest-risk to validate hypothesis.
kevin: tried that — `workspace_reuse=true` reduces mem spike by ~40% but we still see occasional spikes when multiple long seqs arrive concurrently and kv eviction causes temporary peak to allocate new buffers.
carmen: what about moving some KV pages to CPU (spill-to-host) earlier under pressure? we already have a soft-threshold that triggers async spill at 75% but seems too late.
kevin: agree. nvprof shows host<->device memcpy spikes coincide with spill operations; if we spill earlier we might avoid the fallback but pay latency for memcpy. tradeoff needs testing.
perf-bot: Telemetry snapshot (last 2h): avg batch size 178, p95 seq len 1600, kv hitrate 82%, OOM events: 3 (24GB fleet), kernel_fallback_rate: 0.7% -> target to reduce to <0.1%.
ops-bot: FYI I created a canary job: `canary/2125554321-kv-spill-early` with config: `spill_threshold=60, workspace_reuse=true, batch_growth_limit=256`.
maya: proposal: 3-step experiment
1) enable `workspace_reuse=true` globally on canary
2) lower `spill_threshold` to 60% and measure p99 mem and memcpy overhead
3) add an allocator tuning: `slab_size_hint` for long-seq heavy queues (reduce per-request small allocs)
sanjay: implementation detail: allocator change is a one-line heuristic in the slab allocator — pick slab bucket by expected_seq_len instead of request_size. I can draft patch. Pseudocode:

```
if (expected_seq_len > 1024) slab = large_seq_slab;
else slab = default_slab;
```
kevin: also need to adjust kernel selector to prefer smaller-kernel chained calls when mem headroom is under 12% instead of immediately switching to generic kernel. current threshold seems too aggressive.
carmen: +1. maybe add an intermediate fallback: compact-kernel (reuses smaller ephemeral buffers) before generic.
maya: can we add quick telemetry flags to track: `eviction_count`, `mem_headroom_pct`, `kernel_choice` per inference? that'll help correlate.
perf-bot: Added new metrics to the canary job: `eviction_count`, `mem_headroom_pct`, `kernel_choice`. Dashboards auto-created at /dash/canary/2125554321
kevin: timeline for work
- today: run canary with `workspace_reuse=true` + `spill_threshold=60`
- tomorrow: sanjay lands allocator slab hint PR on canary
- after: change kernel selector threshold + add compact-kernel option
maya: if the canary reduces kernel_fallback_rate to <0.1% without >3% latency regression, we roll to dedicated 24GB fleet.
sanjay: I'll open PR and add a small perf test. ETA EOD.
kevin: thanks. attaching small nvprof snippet and the loadgen config in CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/2125554321/prof.zip
carmen: one more ask — when testing, include a workload with intermittent KV-heavy bursts (simulate many cache misses). that was the trigger in production.
kevin: will do. I'll post quick results here once canary runs for 2h. :rocket:
